| [THEORY-1942](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1942.md) | Williams holds that agent-regret, a first-person regret expressed in a willingness to repair, is fitting for harm one caused without fault, so that a special relation to an outcome survives the finding that it was not one's fault; and on his later reading, morality keeps its immunity to luck only by ceasing to be the supreme kind of value (as reported by Nelkin) |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1945](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1945.md) | Tessman argues that oppression burdens the moral goodness of the oppressed both by preventing some virtues from developing and by requiring others, burdened virtues, that enable survival of or resistance to oppression while detracting from their bearer's own flourishing, so that eudaimonism must allow virtues disjoined from their bearer's well-being |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1946](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1946.md) v2 | Rubel, Castro and Pham argue that agency laundering is a distinct wrong of accountability: an agent responsible for a domain makes a process, person or technology partly causally responsible for outcomes in it, ascribes it morally relevant qualities, and so obscures its own causal role and forestalls others' demands for an account, a wrong possible while the agent meets its substantive role responsibilities and one that ordinary algorithm use need not commit |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1948](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1948.md) | Liedo, Van Grunsven and Marin argue that paid care workers' emotional labor is prone to exploitation because care duties are allocated by what Tronto calls privileged irresponsibility, that workers' satisfaction in caring can mask the exploitation, and that care robots assessed only by design, as Care-Centred Value-Sensitive Design assesses them, can sustain or newly enable that irresponsibility, letting employers and governments avoid reallocating care responsibilities |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1950](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1950.md) | Smith argues that answerability is the only kind of moral responsibility: attributability without answerability is not responsibility, accountability is answerability where a specific obligation to others has been violated, and differences in warranted response belong to the ethics of blame, not to distinct conceptions of responsibility |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1952](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1952.md) | In CLINIC v. Rubio the Southern District of New York held that the State Department's 2026 policy ordering consular officers to refuse immigrant visas to nationals of 75 countries, whatever individualized assessment found of their eligibility, made those determinations irrelevant to the outcome, was contrary to the bar on nationality discrimination and to the rule that refusals rest on grounds the law sets out, and exceeded the Secretary of State's authority, and vacated it with the refusals based solely on it | Catholic Legal Immigration Network, Inc. v. Rubio, ECF No. 83 (S.D.N.Y. 21 August 2026), [LIT-2727](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2727.md), read in [NOTE-2054](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2054.md). Officers were to refuse "regardless of whether" an individualized assessment found the applicant eligible, so that "whatever determinations they make as to eligibility ... are ultimately irrelevant. The outcome is predetermined." Held unlawful under §§ 1152(a)(1)(A), 1201(g) and 1104(a), not under the public-charge provision. Filed as grounds of [CLAIM-745](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-745.md), a documented specimen of it, by a note on that claim. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1958](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1958.md) | Miller, as Shaw-Young reports his 2007 statement, holds that remedial responsibility for a bad situation is assigned through several distinct connections to it, moral responsibility, outcome responsibility, causal responsibility, benefit, capacity and community, so that it need not fall on whoever caused the situation or was at fault | Shaw-Young (2008), [LIT-2773](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2773.md), read in part in [NOTE-2064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2064.md), as the weak read neighbour of Miller 2001 ([LIT-2755](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2755.md)). It corroborates the second half of [CLAIM-717](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-717.md), which does not rest on it: a remedial duty can fall on a faultless agent. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1959](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1959.md) | Locke argues in the Second Treatise that because no one has an absolute arbitrary power over his own life no one can by compact or consent give another such power, except where life is forfeited by a fault deserving death, so that the legislative, holding only the joint power its members could transfer, cannot be absolutely arbitrary over their lives and fortunes and holds a fiduciary power the people may resume when the trust is breached | Locke, Two Treatises (1689), Second Treatise, [LIT-2738](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2738.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2077](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2077.md) on the sections the exchange names. "No body can give more power than he has himself" (§23); "no body has an absolute arbitrary power over himself" (§135); the legislative is "only a fiduciary power" (§149). It corroborates the form of [CLAIM-720](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-720.md)'s argument and qualifies it: the ground is power over one's own life, and forfeiture is allowed (a note on that claim). "The people shall be judge" (§240) of a trustee's breach corroborates [CLAIM-727](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-727.md)'s refusal of self-certifying authority. It bears on [QUESTION-481](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-481.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1960](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1960.md) | Pettit proposes that a state is legitimate insofar as it imposes its order under popular control, and that the people control the state insofar as they have an individualized, unconditioned and efficacious influence over it that pushes it in a direction they find acceptable, realized by individual contestation, a resistive citizenry and channels of influence insulated from electoral pressures and private lobbies | Pettit, On the People's Terms (2012), [LIT-2760](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2760.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2047](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2047.md) from the publisher's openings of three parts: people control the state "just insofar as they have an individualized, unconditioned and efficacious influence that pushes it in a direction that they find acceptable". It bears on [QUESTION-482](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-482.md) (insulation of influence as a condition of independence). Proposed: the argument is unread. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1962](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1962.md) | Calabresi and Melamed propose that law protects an entitlement by a property rule, under which it is taken only by a purchase its holder agrees to, a liability rule, under which it may be taken on payment of a collectively determined value, or an inalienability rule, under which its transfer is forbidden, and that criminal sanctions serve partly to deter takers from converting property rules into liability rules by taking first and paying after | Calabresi & Melamed (1972), [LIT-2749](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2749.md), read in [NOTE-2070](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2070.md). Who holds an entitlement is decided first; how it is protected is a second-order decision among property, liability and inalienability rules, chosen mainly by the cost of market and collective valuation. §V: a thief charged only the value of what he took would "convert all property rule entitlements into liability rule entitlements", so punishment adds "an undefinable kicker". It is the mechanism [CLAIM-734](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-734.md) states, filed as that claim's grounds by a note on it. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1964](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1964.md) | Nickel and Etinson characterize human rights as plural, universal, high-priority rights held independently of whether local law, practice or morality recognizes them, deny that inalienability, minimalism or a political function belongs to the concept, and report that the grounds offered for them vary and that agency and dignity each seem to need supplementing | Nickel & Etinson, SEP "Human Rights" (2024 revision), [LIT-2743](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2743.md), read in [NOTE-2042](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2042.md). People have human rights "independently of whether such rights are present in the practices, morality, or law of their country"; "It is doubtful that all human rights are inalienable". It bears on [QUESTION-486](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-486.md), supplying the independence the question wants and qualifying its reliance on inalienability. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1965](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1965.md) | Waldron and Penner present private property as a system of rules assigning contested resources to the decisional authority of particular individuals, who may decide without explanation and whether or not others are affected, so that it is continually in need of public justification, and analyse default title as one Hohfeldian liberty, one claim-right and two powers, to license and to transfer | Waldron & Penner, SEP "Property and Ownership" (2026 revision), [LIT-2744](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2744.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2050](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2050.md) (§§1–2). Private property assigns resources "to the decisional authority of particular individuals", who act "without giving anyone else an explanation", so it "is continually in need of public justification". It bears on [QUESTION-481](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-481.md) (who decides, by regime) and [QUESTION-480](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-480.md) (authority that owes no account). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1967](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1967.md) | Scanlon holds that contractualism explains the Hohfeldian structure of moral rights, claims, liberties and powers including a promisee's power to release the promisor, by the reasons people have to insist on principles with that structure, without taking rights as basic, so that it matters little which parts of the structure are called rights | Scanlon, "Reply to Leif Wenar" (2013), [LIT-2746](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2746.md), read in [NOTE-2075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2075.md). "Contractualism seeks to explain not only first-order claim rights but also powers"; the promisee's power of release is explained by the reasons both parties have to insist on Principle F's consent condition. Filed as grounds of [CLAIM-735](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-735.md), whose premise it is, by a note on that claim; it corroborates [CLAIM-743](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-743.md) for promises, and bears on [QUESTION-483](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-483.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1971](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1971.md) | Ashford and Mulgan report Scanlon's contractualism as holding an act wrong when it would be disallowed by any set of principles that no one could reasonably reject as a basis for informed, unforced general agreement, judged only by individuals' reasons for objecting to a principle and its alternatives, without aggregating lesser complaints against a weightier one, and covering only what we owe to one another | Ashford & Mulgan, SEP "Contractualism" (2018 revision), [LIT-2768](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2768.md), read in [NOTE-2043](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2043.md) as the neighbour of Scanlon (1998), [LIT-2721](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2721.md). It quotes the book's formula (p. 153) and individualist restriction (p. 229). It bears on [QUESTION-483](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-483.md) (contractualism's scope and inputs), on [QUESTION-484](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-484.md) (rejection is judged against alternatives) and on [QUESTION-485](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-485.md) (legitimacy as justifiability to each). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1972](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1972.md) | In Fuentes v. Shevin the Supreme Court held that prejudgment replevin statutes letting goods be seized from their possessor on a private party's ex parte application, without a prior opportunity to be heard, deny due process, because the hearing must come when the deprivation can still be prevented and no later hearing or damage award can undo a deprivation already made, whether or not the possessor would have prevailed | Fuentes v. Shevin, 407 U.S. 67 (1972), [LIT-2735](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2735.md), read in [NOTE-2072](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2072.md). The opportunity to be heard must be "granted at a time when the deprivation can still be prevented"; "no later hearing and no damage award can undo the fact" of the taking; the right "does not depend upon an advance showing that one will surely prevail". It is filed as grounds of [CLAIM-723](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-723.md), which cites it, by a note on that claim, and corroborates by analogy [CLAIM-734](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-734.md), which does not rest on it: after-the-fact remedies are no substitute for the prior opportunity. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1973](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1973.md) | Strawson holds that holding people morally responsible consists in the reactive attitudes, which rest on a demand for goodwill or regard; that pleas of excuse leave the agent a full participant while pleas of exemption suspend the attitudes toward the agent; and that a general thesis of determinism neither does nor could rationally undermine the framework of these attitudes | Strawson (1962), [LIT-2679](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2679.md), read in full in [NOTE-2058](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2058.md). It bears on [QUESTION-068](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-068.md): exemption is a condition on holding responsible that ownership of a will does not supply. It qualifies [CLAIM-708](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-708.md) (see the NOTE) without a relation. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1974](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1974.md) | Shoemaker holds that moral responsibility comes in three independent types, attributability, answerability and accountability, grounded in the capacities for quality of character, quality of judgment and quality of regard and each answered by its own family of responses, anger belonging to accountability | Shoemaker (2019), [LIT-2766](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2766.md), read in part in [NOTE-2048](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2048.md), as the read neighbour of Shoemaker 2011 ([LIT-2777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2777.md)). It bears on [QUESTION-476](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-476.md): one kind of blame can be withheld while another is kept. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1975](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1975.md) | Stern argues that Darwall's account, on which moral obligation consists in what persons have legitimate second-personal authority to demand of one another rather than in actual demands, cannot explain obligations to aid a sufferer who makes no demand, so that wronging, or exclusionary reasons, may suffice for obligation without second-personal authority | Stern (2014), [LIT-2767](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2767.md), read in full in [NOTE-2065](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2065.md), as the read neighbour of Darwall 2006 ([LIT-2756](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2756.md)). It bears on [QUESTION-480](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-480.md) (to whom and why answerability is owed) and corroborates the clause of [CLAIM-738](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-738.md) that an asserted demand has no warrant of its own. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1977](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1977.md) | Scanlon now holds that an act is wrong when someone could reasonably reject, on personal reasons weighed against others' opposing reasons, any principle permitting it, that besides the wrong of not complying with an established and needed practice there is a distinct wrong of failing to do one's part in establishing a needed norm, and that the judgments of sufficiency and relevance this rests on are substantive, which weakens the view's reductive explanatory power | Scanlon, "Contractualism and Intuitionism" (2025 draft), [LIT-2741](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2741.md), read in [NOTE-2051](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2051.md). Interactive reasonable rejection; the Principle of Established Practices (p. 21) and the distinct wrong of "failing to do one's part in getting such a norm established" (p. 22); the bilateral reading and the 1998 account of aggregation retracted; relevance "broadly speaking a moral question". It corroborates [CLAIM-729](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-729.md), which rests on [CLAIM-560](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-560.md) and A's report, not on this paper, and bears on [QUESTION-483](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-483.md) and [QUESTION-484](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-484.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1982](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1982.md) | Dirty hands are coherent, on Eggert's account: when two actual duties conflict, an act that is all things considered permissible, even required, can remain wrong, because the overridden duty survives as a moral remainder that makes remorse apt and can ground duties of apology or compensation | Eggert (2023; issue 2025), [LIT-2724](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2724.md), read in full in [NOTE-2040](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2040.md). The account concerns the agent's remainder, not the arranger's wrong. It notes in passing that paradigm cases involve someone else creating the predicament, and leaves open whether they always do. It is filed without relations: the claim it was registered for, [CLAIM-708](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-708.md), cites it for nothing, and the paper does not carry the second-order wrong. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1984](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1984.md) | Hohfeld proposes that the word right in judicial reasoning covers several distinct legal relations, which reduce to eight fundamental conceptions, claim and duty, privilege and no-right, power and liability, immunity and disability, each with a correlative held by another party and an opposite, and that a legal power, volitional control over a change in legal relations, is distinct from the physical power to perform the acts that exercise it and from the privilege of performing them | Hohfeld (1913), [LIT-2762](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2762.md), read in [NOTE-2071](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2071.md). Eight conceptions in four correlative and four opposite pairs, "the lowest common denominators of the law"; a claim persists though the holder's own privilege is extinguished; legal power is distinct from "the physical power to do the things necessary" for its exercise. Filed as grounds of [CLAIM-722](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-722.md), whose separation of physical from normative power is A87's restatement of it, by a note on that claim; it corroborates [CLAIM-738](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-738.md), which does not rest on it, on the independence of normative positions. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1987](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1987.md) | King holds that responsibility as attributability carries desert as fittingness and responsibility as accountability carries desert as fairness, which depends also on the blamer's standing and the agent's opportunity to avoid sanction, and that neither notion of desert extends to the other face | King (2013), [LIT-2770](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2770.md), read in full in [NOTE-2053](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2053.md), as the read neighbour of Watson 1996 ([LIT-2718](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2718.md)). It bears on [QUESTION-068](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-068.md): accountability needs fairness and standing, which ownership of the act does not supply. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1988](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1988.md) | Wenar argues that Scanlon's contractualism cannot, from its principles and their justifications alone, say which principles ascribe rights or to whom obligations are owed, and that because it must also account for rights of authority to change what is owed it must be a multi-level theory, of authority over as well as of owing to | Wenar (2013), "Rights and What We Owe to Each Other", [LIT-2758](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2758.md), read in [NOTE-2038](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2038.md). Scanlon's principles are "principles of wrongness, not of wronging"; "Rights of authority explain who can change what we owe to each other and how", so contractualism "must be a multi-level theory". It bears on [QUESTION-483](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-483.md) as a published form of its second option, and corroborates [CLAIM-735](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-735.md), which does not rest on it, in separating the justification of what is owed from authority to change it. Scanlon's reply is [LIT-2746](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2746.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1990](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1990.md) | Shue argues that rights to subsistence, security and liberty are basic rights, so that subsistence rights share the highest priority with security and liberty, that defending them chiefly means answering the objection that their correlative duties ask too much of others, and that those duties are of avoidance, protection and aid | Shue, Basic Rights (1980; 40th-anniversary edition 2020), [LIT-2750](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2750.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2076](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2076.md): the Introduction and index of the publisher's sample. The triad of duties is given by the index ("of avoidance, protection and aid") and is unread in the text, hence Proposed. It corrects [TERM-085](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-085.md)'s attribution of "respect, protect and fulfil" to Shue (a note on that term). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1992](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1992.md) | Wenar and Cruft hold that rights are complexes of four Hohfeldian incidents, privilege, claim, power and immunity, which combine into molecular rights including second-order powers to alter incidents and others' authority, while the function of rights, whether to give control over another's duty, to further the holder's interests or something else, remains contested | Wenar & Cruft, SEP "Rights" (2025 revision), [LIT-2765](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2765.md), read in [NOTE-2035](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2035.md). Molecular rights of Hohfeldian incidents; "Power-rights to alter the authority of others are ... definitive of all developed legal and political systems"; will against interest theory. It corroborates the structural half of [CLAIM-735](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-735.md), which does not rest on it, and bears on [QUESTION-486](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-486.md) (inalienable, forfeitable and waivable rights; moral rights grounded in moral reasons). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1993](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1993.md) | Democracy, on Tronto's account, is the allocation of caring responsibilities in a political community, with equal voice for all in making the allocations; care is misallocated by excluding those one wants to saddle with the hardest tasks, and by exempting oneself through appeal to more important duties such as protection and production | Tronto (2014), slides, [LIT-2774](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2774.md), read in full in [NOTE-2049](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2049.md), as a read neighbour of Caring Democracy ([LIT-2669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2669.md), Unavailable). Exemption and exclusion corroborate the upstream half of [CLAIM-707](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-707.md), which does not rest on them: parties with standing shed care obligations onto others. Equal voice in the allocating bears on [QUESTION-487](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-487.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1997](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1997.md) | Dekker and Nyce argue that a just-culture scheme that sorts errors into honest mistakes, at-risk behaviour and recklessness treats culpability as an objective fact, when whether a response is just depends on where one stands in the organization's hierarchy and who gets to say, so that the scheme can carry blame along lines of power | Dekker and Nyce (2013), [LIT-2786](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2786.md), read in [NOTE-2080](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2080.md), as the neighbour of Dekker (2007), [LIT-2781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2781.md). It bears on [QUESTION-476](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-476.md)'s third answer, that "blameless" in practice relocates blame, and corroborates the mechanism of [CLAIM-750](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-750.md), that whoever governs a review shapes what it finds, for hospitals. The wording is the filer's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2001.md) | Meaningfulness is a dimension of a good life distinct from happiness and morality, arising when a person loves objects worthy of love and engages with them actively | Wolf's thesis itself, filed beside [THEORY-1836](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1836.md), which reports that she argues it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md): each promoted attribution gets its wider thesis filed beside it, Proposed). The attribution is Active on [NOTE-1949](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1949.md)'s reading of the 2007 Tanner Lectures; the thesis waits on the standard of worth it needs and Wolf says she does not supply. | Proposed |
